ai.title: GPT-6.1 Terra fast-tier routing constants
ai.summary: The shared model catalog in `common` adds `FREEBUFF_GPT_61_TERRA_FAST_UPSTREAM_ORDER` and `FREEBUFF_GPT_61_TERRA_FAST_MAX_PRICE` to support the first-thread A/B experiment for GPT-6.1 Terra. The routing order prioritizes OpenAI's `openai/fast` endpoint with the standard tier as a backup, ensuring a capacity refusal results in a slower turn rather than a failure. The price ceiling is set to $2.50/$12.50 per million tokens to strictly exceed the fast tier's $2/$10 card while remaining below any higher bands.
ai.evidence: The diff adds two new constants in `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts`: `FREEBUFF_GPT_61_TERRA_FAST_UPSTREAM_ORDER` (defining the routing sequence for OpenAI's `fast` tier) and `FREEBUFF_GPT_61_TERRA_FAST_MAX_PRICE` (the associated cost fence).
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show where the server-side logic currently reads these constants to route A/B traffic to the new fast-tier configuration.

eli5.text: The shared model catalog now defines two new rules for a specific speed-focused setting of the GPT-6.1 Terra AI model. These rules tell the system to prioritize a faster service endpoint, with a standard backup option available if the fast one is busy, and they set a strict spending limit to keep costs controlled. This is an internal configuration update that prepares the system for a controlled test of this model; it does not change any model availability, pricing, or features for you right now.
